- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–3% to match recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply a “cool-down” correction of -1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for sudden reversal in forecast slope and reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day after sentiment drop.
- Model tends to overfit short-term momentum; for 30-day forecasts, apply a 1–2% mean reversion bias toward recent 7-day average if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 5+ days, model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to account for volatility.
